summary: Satoshi Naiki is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Kyoto University, where he later served as an assistant professor (attested 2016-2020).

Satya Narayan Goenka (1924-2013) was a Buddhist and religious studies teacher. He studied under Sayagyi U Ba Khin from around 1955 to 1969, founded the Vipassana Research Institute in 1985, and taught numerous students, including Joseph Goldstein and Sharon Salzberg.

Satya Swarup Misra (born 1935) is an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and as Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University.

Satya Vrat Shastri (1930-2021) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned degrees at the University of the Punjab and Banaras Hindu University. He held key posts at the University of Delhi, including department head, and served as Vice-Chancellor of Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya.

Satyendra Nath Bose (1894-1974) studied at Presidency University and University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at the University of Calcutta and University of Dhaka, and later served as Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956-1958).
Saubhagya Pradhananga works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Attested in 2018, Pradhananga served as Chief of the National Archives of Nepal and on the editorial board of Documenta Nepalica.

Sayadaw U Pandita (1921-2016) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mahasi Sayadaw and Nandasiri Sayadaw. He taught at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha, succeeded Mahasi Sayadaw from 1982 to 1991, and founded and served as abbot of Panditarama Meditation Center.

Sayadaw U Sīlānanda (1927-2005) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mahasi Sayadaw and U Paññāvanta. He held leadership roles at Mahavijjodaya Chaung, Abyarama Shwegu Taik, Dhammānanda Vihara, and served as Chancellor of the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University.

Sayadaw U Thittila (1896-1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University. He served as a librarian for the Adyar Library and the Buddhist Society, and as Lecturer in Buddhist Philosophy at the University of Rangoon.

Sayagyi U Ba Khin (1899-1971) was a religious and Buddhist studies figure. He studied under Saya Thetgyi from around 1937 to 1945, founded the International Meditation Centre, and taught teachers including Satya Narayan Goenka and Mother Sayamagyi.
Sayaka Sonoda completed a PhD at Toyo University (attested 2015-2016), studying under doctoral supervisor Shinobu Yamaguchi and co-supervisor Shogo Watanabe.
Sayori Tsubota is an Indologist who was a PhD student at Osaka University (attested 2020) and is attested as a JSPS Postdoctoral Fellow (PD) at Tohoku University in 2026.

Scott A. Mitchell specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne and has held professorial and presidential appointments at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and the Numata Center.
Scott DeLancey (born 1949) is a scholar in linguistics and Tibetology who studied under Yungdrung Manang. He held a post at the University of Oregon around 1982.
Scott Hurley is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied under Elizabeth Harrison and completed his PhD at the University of Arizona in 2001.

Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. After earning his doctorate at the Australian National University in 2011, he held positions at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, the Australian National University, and the University of Manchester.

Sean D. Gaffney is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, where he was also attested in 1996, and studied under scholars including Philip Denwood and Alexander Piatigorsky.

Sebastian Nehrdich specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed an MA at the University of Hamburg, was an exchange student at Kyoto University, and held posts at Tohoku University and the University of Hamburg (attested 2024-2026).
Sebastian Pole works in Indology and related fields. He completed his studies at the East West College of Herbalism, the London College of Oriental Medicine, and the College of Ayurveda.
See Mui Yian is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).
